issue.title: Add confirmed conversation rewind from structured chat messages
issue.body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 8 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​844 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​16 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​828 |
| Prod | 11 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​570 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​109 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​461 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

You can now choose **Revert to here** on a user message in structured chat, confirm how many messages will be discarded, and continue from the earlier conversation. The selected message and everything after it are removed; file changes on disk stay intact.

Before, user messages had no way to rewind the conversation. After, hovering or focusing a user row exposes the action, and a destructive confirmation explains what will be lost before anything is sent.

## What Changed

- Added the user-row action with specific explanations when the session is busy, unwritable, or does not support rewind.
- Connected it to the merged rewind backend using the existing runtime target and mutation envelope. The copy map covers exactly the backend's nine reason codes at compile time, with a fallback for an unknown reason from a newer host.
- Wait for the host's conversation reset before clearing stale transcript state, draft text, and attachments. Ordinary reconnects preserve drafts.
- Keep sending and queued-message retries blocked while a rewind is pending or its outcome is unknown. The uncertainty message explicitly says the rewind may have completed and that sending stays blocked until the outcome is resolved.

## Why

This gives users a confirmed way to discard later conversation history. Restoring the removed prompt into the composer is deliberately omitted: it would race the host's conversation reset and the composer remount, risking stale text or attachments being restored after the reset. The composer starts empty after a successful rewind.

## Linked Issue

Coordinator-dispatched structured chat rewind task; no issue URL was supplied. Builds on merged backend PR #19235.

## Visual Proof

These uncropped screenshots were captured during this branch's earlier background Electron validation on macOS. They show the action and confirmation before the final copy wording was refined; they are not evidence of a completed provider rewind. That validation exercised pending/ready states and cancellation preserving the transcript and draft. No pre-change screenshot was captured.

![User-row rewind action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5f40dfd-8e98-47a5-9291-a45c82321540)

![Destructive confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ee5e7b2-cf95-41cc-9f99-5665c40416c7)

## Testing

- [x] After merging main, 79 focused tests passed across eight suites: rewind hook, action, accepted-message target selection, pane/epoch reset, session controller, recovery outbox, and runtime client.
- [x] Added nine cases using the real backend reason constant; the updated rewind-hook suite passed all 35 tests (88 distinct focused cases in total).
- [x] Changed-file oxlint and whitespace checks passed.
- [x] Confirmed merge commit `5b0a10493d` has two parents and includes backend commit `ce4a3a4186`; inspected committed user-row and English-copy integration.
- [ ] Typecheck is coordinator-owned; it was not run here. CI covers broader checks.
- [ ] A confirmed live provider rewind and Linux/Windows/SSH UI validation remain untested here; automated cases cover remote target routing and both response/reset orderings.

## Review

The five existing UI commits are preserved. Main was merged, not rebased. Timestamp PR #19218 is still open and `NativeChatMessageTimestamp.tsx` is absent from the merged main revision; this PR supplies one user-row hover strip for future composition.

The feature diff is renderer-only, with no provider, journal, mobile, file rollback, or wire-contract changes. Folder workspaces retain the existing runtime routing, and remote capability negotiation comes from the merged backend implementation.

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused renderer change with before/after behavior and rationale described.
- [x] Self-reviewed against the merged backend contract.
- [x] Cross-platform and SSH/remote impact considered.
- [ ] Coordinator typecheck and live provider integration validation complete.

comments.body:
## Manual UI validation — Electron, live providers

Ran this branch's build on a fresh isolated dev profile (hidden window, CDP screenshots only) against a **live Codex app-server session (GPT-6-Astra)** and a **live Claude structured session (Opus)** in a folder workspace. The rewind was actually executed end-to-end against the provider, not simulated.

### What the screenshots show

![Hovering a user message in dark theme reveals a single undo affordance under that bubble; the other user messages stay clean.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dbfa959-343f-41a6-8c07-fb2caa3b3c21)
*1. Dark theme — hovering one user message reveals the "Revert to here" affordance under that bubble only (the other rows stay at opacity 0).*

![The affordance rendered dimmed under a user message while the pane shows "Working for 33s".](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a49b5897-2175-4def-9641-2a5744e02c83)
*2. Dark theme — while a turn is running ("Working for 33s") every rewind button is `aria-disabled="true"` and renders dimmed; its title/`aria-description` reads "Wait for the current turn, pending messages, approvals, and background work to finish before rewinding." Clicking it in that state opened no dialog.*

![Modal titled "Revert to here?" over the dark chat pane, with a red "Discard messages" button.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5be7fc5b-630d-4af7-9c1a-b42e7117f236)
*3. Dark theme — the confirmation names the blast radius concretely: "Discard this message and every later message (6 in total)? This cannot be undone. Your composer draft and attachments will be cleared. File changes on disk will be kept."*

![The dark chat pane back to its full transcript with all four prompts and replies present.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cae9c1f6-22b8-40e2-9e53-19ec0f4a243f)
*4. Dark theme — after pressing Cancel the transcript is untouched: all four prompts and their replies are still there and the buttons re-enable.*

![Light theme chat pane with the undo affordance revealed under the second user message.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa95ac62-1197-4aad-aef8-89b680009e46)
*5. Light theme — same hover affordance, adequate contrast against the muted user bubble.*

![Light theme "Revert to here?" modal with a red "Discard messages" button.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a32f2d0e-bd19-434e-8785-408c5d4493b9)
*6. Light theme — the same confirmation, destructive styling on "Discard messages" and ghost styling on "Cancel".*

![Light theme chat pane with the composer containing the text DRAFT-SHOULD-BE-CLEARED-AFTER-REVERT.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c03f826-46a2-4cb9-9686-73ed59da98e3)
*7. Light theme — a composer draft typed immediately before the real revert, so the "your draft will be cleared" promise can be checked.*

![Light theme chat pane showing only the first prompt and its ONE reply, with an empty composer.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/661ff6a1-2f22-4fe3-9b72-5fafbb8507ec)
*8. Light theme — after confirming: the transcript is truncated back to the first exchange, the six later messages are gone, no stale rows, and the composer draft is cleared and re-enabled.*

![Dark theme chat pane showing the same truncated transcript.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37ef87fb-5d45-438c-89bf-c0573d28e800)
*9. The same post-revert state in dark theme.*

![Dark theme chat pane where a new FOUR prompt and reply follow the retained first exchange.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa04b722-215b-49f4-8334-750bb9ea76c6)
*10. Sending works normally after the revert — the new turn appends onto the retained history, so the pane is not left wedged.*

![Claude Chat pane with the undo affordance showing a keyboard focus ring.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b406b30-bb7f-4734-95e3-854eb13efa84)
*11. The affordance is keyboard reachable (revealed by `group-focus-within`, focus ring visible) and is present on Claude structured sessions too, not just Codex.*

### Result per guard rail

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Appears on user messages, discoverable but not intrusive | Pass — one button per user message, none on assistant rows, hidden at rest and revealed on hover or keyboard focus |
| 2 | Disabled while a turn is running | Pass — proven live (screenshot 2); the disabled button also swallows the click |
| 2b | Disabled while the session is not writable | **Not exercised** — see gaps below |
| 3 | Confirmation names what is discarded | Pass — "(6 in total)", counted correctly as the 3 user + 3 assistant messages from the target onward |
| 4 | Cancel changes nothing | Pass — transcript, message count and enabled state all identical after Cancel |
| 5 | Confirm truncates and reloads cleanly | Pass — real provider rewind; 6 messages gone, 1 exchange retained, no stale rows, draft cleared |
| 6 | A refusal is legible | **Not induced** — see gaps below |
| 7 | Correct in light and dark | Pass — both themes for affordance and confirmation, post-revert captured in both |

### Two small things worth a look (neither blocks)

1. **Misleading composer copy while the confirmation is open.** With the dialog up, the composer is disabled and its placeholder reads *"Input is held by another device."* Nothing is held by another device — the local rewind is pending. It reverts to "Send a message…" on cancel, and the dialog does not cover the composer, so it is visible.
2. **The retained turn loses its status row.** Before the rewind the first exchange showed "Worked for 4s ›"; after the reload that row is gone for the retained history (screenshots 9/10), while the new post-rewind turn has one. Cosmetic, but the disclosure for retained turns disappears.

### What I could not exercise

- **Not-writable disabled state.** On this machine both available providers stayed writable; the only ways I found to force a non-writable session were killing the provider child process or a second client taking the session, neither of which I was willing to do on a shared machine. The busy/turn-running half of that guard rail is proven; the not-writable half is not.
- **A refusal path.** Both providers here report `rewind: supported` (Codex on the paginated history mode, Claude via its transcript leaf), and the app blocks concurrent mutation while the dialog is open, so I could not naturally reach `history-not-paginated`, `stale-epoch`, `provider-refused`, or `outcome-unknown`. Every refusal I saw in the code has copy behind it, but **no refusal string was observed on screen** — please treat requirement 6 as unvalidated rather than passed.

## Status: ready for review

Depends on #19235 (merged). This is the affordance that calls it.

### Plan review
Reviewed before any code was written. **APPROVE WITH AMENDMENTS**, all applied. The one that mattered most: **`outcome-unknown` must not read as a clean failure.** It means the revert may or may not have completed and sending is blocked until it resolves — phrasing that as "rewind failed" would mislead a user at the worst possible moment. Also required: pin the reason vocabulary at compile time so a future tenth reason **breaks the build** rather than silently falling through to a generic message, and use the specific reason in disabled-state copy so a legacy-history session says *why* rather than a bare "unavailable".

### Built against the real contract
The copy map was written before #19235 merged, against reason codes relayed by the coordinator. After the merge it was re-verified against the **actual** `AgentSessionRewindReason` union on main, with an exhaustive compile-time pin. Sibling branches were deliberately **not** merged in to make it compile early — that would have put another lane's unreviewed commits inside this PR.

### Verification
- Central typecheck: **exit 0**.
- Merged with `origin/main`, two parents verified; the rewind backend is an ancestor.
- 79 focused tests plus a 35-test hook suite, changed-file oxlint clean.

### Manual UI validation — a real rewind was performed
Fresh isolated dev profile, hidden renderer, CDP-only, driving **a live Codex app-server session and a live Claude structured session**. **11 captioned screenshots attached above.** Proven live, not simulated:
- the affordance appears per user message, hidden until hover or keyboard focus
- `aria-disabled` with busy copy while a turn runs, and it **swallows the click**
- the confirmation names the blast radius concretely — *"6 in total"* = 3 user + 3 assistant
- **Cancel changes nothing**
- a **real provider rewind** truncated the transcript back to the first exchange, cleared the composer draft, left no stale rows, and **sending worked afterwards**
- correct in both themes

### Deliberate omission
Restoring the reverted prompt back into the composer is **not** implemented. Doing so races the `epoch_changed` remount that a successful rewind triggers; the plan review agreed omitting it was the right call rather than adding a race to save a paste.

### Process deviations, stated plainly
- **The review loop's `$orchestration` arm was not used.** Nested worker depth is 1 in this install, so a dispatched worker cannot dispatch its own workers (`nested_worker_depth_exceeded`). The UI validation lane was run directly by the coordinator at depth 0.
- **`readiness-checklist`'s severity-counsel step was unavailable** for the same depth reason, and is recorded as unavailable rather than reported as a verdict.

### Known-red, not caused by this PR
`structured-agent-session-adoption-replay.test.ts:188` fails on a clean detached `origin/main` checkout — reproduced independently by two lanes. Pre-existing break on main, deliberately not touched.
